title: Recommendation Inspector — flow & annotated wireframes (WIP)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working doc for the "Recommendation Inspector" — an inline/side-panel UI in the Optimize console that lets engineers preview, simulate, and apply per-route inference recommendations (batching presets, prefix caching candidates, and quantization profiles). The goal is a lightweight, explorable UI that reduces the time from suggestion -> safe rollout while preserving easy rollback and quality checks.

Audience:
- Product and UX (primary): to iterate on flows and microcopy
- Eng/Applied ML: to validate simulation outputs and add telemetry hooks
- Solutions/SE: to use the UI during customer onboarding

High-level flow (user story):
1) User opens Console > Optimize > Recommendations.
2) Clicks a route or model row -> Recommendation Inspector slides over from the right.
3) Inspector shows: Summary, Simulation, Sample outputs, Apply & Rollout controls.
4) User toggles candidate suggestions to preview expected cost and latency delta, inspects sample outputs for quality regression, runs a simulated canary (locally or via synthetic traffic), and either applies change immediately or schedules a staged rollout.

Key UX goals / constraints:
- Fast preview: show estimated latency and token cost immediately using cached telemetry + heuristics.
- Local quality checks: side-by-side sample responses for baseline vs proposed change with quick quality flags (BLEU-like heuristics + human-check tag).
- Simulation: a configurable simulator that replays representative traces (user can pick a timeframe) and produces distributions, p99 shift, and estimated spend delta.
- Rollouts: support canary (X%), auto-fallback, and linkable audit trail.
- Safe-by-default: defaults to non-destructive previews — applying requires an explicit confirmation and notes.

Annotated wireframe notes (low-fi):
[Inspector header]
- Left: route name (clickable to open route details) + current model variant badge
- Center: concise one-line summary: "3 suggestions — 2 high-confidence" + quick badges (est. -18% cost, +20% tokens/sec)
- Right: compact action set: Save config (copies JSON), Open Simulation, Apply (primary)
[TAB NAV — Summary | Simulation | Samples | Audit]

Summary tab (default):
- Top: "Recommendation stack" list (visual stacked chips):
  * Batching: suggested preset (e.g. steady-200ms batching, 32 token limit) + confidence score
  * Caching: prefix candidate (hash pattern preview) + hit-rate estimate
  * Quantization: suggested profile (int8-llm qlora-ish) + expected throughput boost
- Each suggestion row: small sparkline (latency/cost) + quick toggle (preview on/off).
- Expand row -> show rationale bullets (why suggested, linked traces, sample prompting shapes that benefit).
- Small link: "See full model performance profile" (opens model catalog).

Simulation tab:
- Controls: timeframe picker (last 24h / 7d / custom), sample size slider, synthetic traffic toggle, seed for reproducibility.
- Charts (left-to-right): latency distribution (hist), token throughput over time, cost burn by bucket, p99 delta gauge.
- Key metric cards: est. monthly $ delta, p50/p95/p99 change, expected error rate impact (heuristic).
- CTA: "Run simulation" -> triggers job (shows estimate of runtime). Historical runs shown below with clickable diffs (compare run A/B).

Samples tab:
- Table: Request snippet | Baseline response | Proposed response | Quick diff highlighting tokens added/removed
- Inline quality flags: hallucination heuristic, truncated response indicator, top-token-shift metric.
- Ability to mark sample as "ok" / "fail" (this feeds into quality gating on rollout).

Audit tab:
- Shows previous changes, who applied, applied config JSON, rollout % timeline and final outcome.
- Button: Export audit (CSV).

Wireframe ASCII (very low-fi):
------------------------------------------------------------
| Routes list (left) | Recommendation Inspector (right)       |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------|
| /search            | Header: /search  • model=v1  • 3 recs   |
| /chat              | Tabs: Summary | Simulation | Samples |
| /summarize         | Suggestion 1: batching (preview toggle) |
| ...                | Suggestion 2: caching  (preview toggle) |
|                    | Suggestion 3: quantize (preview toggle) |
|                    | [Run simulation] [Apply] [Save as preset] |
------------------------------------------------------------

Backlog grooming (initial task list):
- UX-374 (JIRA-OPT-9123): Build Summary tab UI + toggle interactions (owner: Diego) — M: 3 sprint days.
- ENG-581: Simulation backend API + sampling endpoint (owner: Evan) — M: 2 sprints. Blocked by infra quota work (INFRA-210).
- ML-223: Quantization candidate scoring function + confidence metric (owner: Linnea) — M: 1.5 sprints.
- QA-88: Regression test harness for sample diffs (owner: qa-team) — M: 5 days.
- UX-382: Keyboard shortcuts & accessibility audit (owner: Amina) — small.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Summary tab shows at least 3 types of recommendations (batching, caching, quantize) with estimated cost and latency deltas computed from the last 7d telemetry.
- Simulation tab executes and returns same metrics displayed by backend job; UI shows run status & results.
- Samples tab shows at least 10 representative request/response pairs, with baseline vs proposed diff and ability to tag.
- Apply flow creates an immutable audit entry with config JSON and optional rollout schedule.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- How to compute "confidence" consistently across different suggestion types? (ML team: propose a small set of calibrated heuristics)
- Should we allow users to edit suggestion parameters in-place (eg. change batching window from 200ms to 150ms) before applying? (Pros: faster tuning. Cons: complexity + validation risk.)
- Simulation cost: do we charge for simulation runs on dedicated accounts? Need biz input.
- Rollout telemetry: do we require a minimum observation window before completing a rollout? (default: 24h)

Telemetry hooks (for eng):
- events: recommendation_preview.open, recommendation_preview.toggle, simulation.run.request, simulation.run.complete, apply.recommendation.start, apply.recommendation.complete, sample.flagged
- properties: route, model_variant, suggestion_type, suggestion_params (as JSON blob), run_id, estimated_savings_pct

Microcopy suggestions:
- Apply button: "Apply with staged rollout" (secondary: "Apply immediately")
- Preview toggle tooltip: "Temporarily simulate this suggestion on your route to preview latency/cost changes without changing production config."

A11y notes:
- Ensure keyboard focus lands in the inspector when opened; escape closes it.
- Charts must have text summaries for screen readers.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Finish high-fidelity mockups for Summary + Samples (Amina + UX).
- Spike: simulation API contract with eng (Evan) — define endpoints and cost estimates.
- ML to provide prototype confidence scoring and sample ranking (Linnea).
- UX to run 2 quick lab sessions with SEs to validate information density.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OPT-781 (design rationale and performance profiles)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/recs-ui/pull/421 (starting scaffold for inspector panel)
- JIRA epic: JIRA-OPT-9123

Notes to self / informal: 
- Keep language simple; SEs prefer "estimated savings" over percent shorthand.
- Consider small CTA "Save as preset" so customers can reuse tuned stacks across routes.
- Potential future: allow multi-route batch apply + dry-run across a chosen subset.

----
Document history (work-in-progress):
- 2025-02-11: initial outline and flow (Amina)
- 2025-02-14: added simulation controls + telemetry hooks (Evan)
- 2025-02-20: added backlog tasks and acceptance criteria (Diego)

END OF WIP
